distinguishing_features: Impressed-current cathodic protection to polarize the titanium anode into the immune potential region
Control loop monitoring potential vs. reference to maintain the potential below the corrosion threshold
Inert anode bed in the anolyte outlet sump as the counter electrode
Reference threshold set at -5 mV vs. SHE
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to prevent electrochemical dissolution of the titanium anode coating in chlor-alkali anolyte without relying on a passive barrier layer
parsed.viable_reason: The stated applied current density of -5 mA/cm² is insufficient to shift the anode potential from +1.5 V to the immune region (below -0.2 V vs. SHE), and the configuration only addresses test coupons in the sump, not the actual anode in the cell.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Since the mechanism is not viable, it cannot be non-obvious; moreover, cathodic protection is a standard corrosion prevention technique, and applying it to a titanium anode in a chlor-alkali cell would be obvious to a skilled engineer if it were feasible.
